title: The 40-Year Farm Stand Dilemma

scenario.title: The 40-Year Farm Stand Dilemma
scenario.setting: Tucked along a winding country highway, the weathered wooden farm stand has operated continuously for 40 years, passed down through three local farming families. A commercial truck stop developer has filed plans to build adjacent to the stand’s small plot, threatening its loyal customer base and long-term viability. The current family owners face an impossible choice: take a substantial buyout or fight to preserve the community landmark they grew up with.

characters.name: Elara
characters.tendencies: She focuses solely on crunching financial numbers, comparing the buyout offer to the stand’s historical revenue to make a data-driven decision.

characters.name: Javi
characters.tendencies: He organizes neighborhood petitions and social media campaigns to rally support for saving the farm stand.

characters.name: Lila
characters.tendencies: She runs the stand’s daily operations, restocks fresh produce, and greets every regular customer by name.

turns.name: Elara
turns.text:
“I’m not leaning on guesswork here—let’s anchor this to hard numbers first. Our five-year average seasonal revenue sits right around $11,900 annually, and this buyout offer is nearly four times that yearly total, which blows past the standard 2x industry benchmark for rural farm stands.”
[pulling a battered solar-powered calculator from her work overalls pocket and tapping the handwritten offer sum against her pre-scrawled annual sales notes]

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Hey there—this weathered family farm stand has been a staple here for 40 years, and it’s at risk of shutting down for good. I’m collecting petition signatures to pressure local leaders to protect these small, neighborhood businesses. Could you take a minute to sign and spread the word to anyone else who cares about keeping our community’s heart alive?
[Tucks a stack of printed petition forms under one arm and holds up a bright homemade flyer decorated with sun-ripened tomatoes and jars of honey.]

turns.name: Lila
turns.text:
Hey there, Mr. Hale! I just restocked those Brandywine heirloom tomatoes you raved about last week—picked fresh straight from the backyard patch at dawn this morning. I also set aside a small carton of our just-harvested blueberries if you want to add something sweet to your order.
[Wiping my sticky, juice-stained hands on my denim overalls and reaching for a sturdy paper grocery bag to pack his chosen produce]

turns.name: Elara
turns.text: “I need to cross-reference this proposed buyout against both our five-year annual average and our peak seasonal sales windows, which make up nearly 70% of our total yearly earnings. A flat one-time offer won’t reflect the full, ongoing value of this 40-year-old stand, so we can’t finalize anything without further number-crunching.” [She pulls a coffee-ringed spiral notebook from her canvas bag, flipping quickly to a page covered in handwritten revenue spreadsheets and circled seasonal sales peaks.]

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Hey Lila, those fresh picked tomatoes are exactly what’ll draw drivers off the highway to listen. I’ve got a fresh stack of hand-printed petitions to rally community support to save the 40-year-old farm stand, and I’d love for you to sign one first before I start passing them around.
[pulling a neat stack of cream-colored petition sheets from my canvas tote and tucking a black ballpoint pen through the top corner before holding the whole set out to her.]

turns.name: Lila
turns.text:
Hey there, Mr. Hale! I just restocked those Brandywine heirloom tomatoes you raved about last week—picked fresh straight from the backyard patch at dawn, and I set out a basket of sun-ripened white peaches too for your weekly morning stop. I saw your petition papers earlier, and I’ll definitely sign one before I head out later today.
[I step out from behind the scuffed farm stand counter, grabbing a crumpled brown paper bag to pack his produce, and nod at the stack of clipboards propped against the jarred jam shelves.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Elara holds the line; the next session's hook waits at the door.
